title: FortiGate 60E to 60F Migration: Three Paths and What Breaks
excerpt: How to move a FortiGate 60E config to a 60F before support ends December 29, 2026: matching FortiOS 7.4, free FortiConverter, header edits, port renames and licenses.

claims.claim: The FortiGate 60E reached end of order on December 29, 2021 and reaches end of support on December 29, 2026.
claims.quote: The FortiGate 60E reached end of order on 29 December 2021 and reaches end of support on 29 December 2026.

claims.claim: The 60E's last service extension date was December 29, 2025.
claims.quote: Its last service extension date passed on 29 December 2025.

claims.claim: Jimber's timeline takes its dates from Fortinet's Product Life Cycle portal.
claims.quote: Source for all dates: Fortinet's official Product Life Cycle portal.

claims.claim: Fortinet's lifecycle portal (Hardware table: Product, EOO, LSED, EOS, Last Supported Software Version) lists the FortiGate-60E with EOO December 29, 2021, LSED December 29, 2025, EOS December 29, 2026 and LSSV 7.4.0. The portal is a JavaScript app; this row was read from its data on October 5, 2026 (portal last updated October 2, 2026).
The FortiGate-60E-POE variant is supported until October 14, 2027.
Fortinet defines the last service extension date as the last date it accepts an extension of a support or security subscription contract.

claims.claim: FortiConverter returns a converted configuration file and a report.
claims.quote: A converted configuration file and report

claims.quote: From FortiOS v7.4.0 and above, the FortiConverter ticket can be opened when going through the initial setup page on the GUI of the FortiGate instead of accessing the portal.

claims.claim: The source unit option is Allow FortiConverter to obtain config file once under System > Settings (search result text for this page).
claims.quote: go to System > Settings and enable "Allow FortiConverter to obtain config file once"

claims.claim: On the target unit, the GUI setup offers Migrate Config with FortiConverter (search result text for this page).
claims.quote: on the GUI startup menu click Begin to start "Migrate Config with FortiConverter"

claims.claim: Managed FortiSwitch, FortiAP, FortiToken and FortiManager upgrades are outside FortiConverter's scope.
claims.quote: The upgrades for managed software or external devices (such as FortiAP, FortiToken, FortiClient EMS, FortiManager, and FortiSwitch) are not supported.

claims.claim: FortiConverter converts hardware switches to software switches when the target cannot support them.
claims.quote: Hardware switches will be converted to software switches where the new target device does not support the hardware switch.

claims.claim: FortiConverter resets the default admin password.
claims.quote: For security purposes, the default admin account password will be reset.

claims.claim: VPN pre-shared keys, certificates and local users generally stay valid if FortiOS is above 5.6.
claims.quote: encrypted secret data, credentials, such as VPN pre-shared keys, certificates, local users, and admin passwords will remain valid after cross-model migration if the FortiOS version is above 5.6.

claims.claim: Fortinet does not support manually modified cross-model configuration files.
claims.quote: Fortinet Support does not provide support for configuration files that were manually modified to migrate a configuration from one FortiGate model to another.

claims.claim: Fortinet's example header swaps an 80F model code for a 100F.
claims.quote: #config-version=FGT80F-7.0.6-FW-build0366-220606:opmode=0:vdom=0:user=admin

claims.claim: A 60F backup on 7.4.11 begins with an FGT60F config-version line.
claims.quote: #config-version=FGT60F-7.4.11-FW-build2878-260126:opmode=0:vdom=0:user=szhao

claims.claim: Owners report the 60E header carries FGT60E and must be changed to FGT60F.
claims.quote: You have to replace the first line in config (part with FGT modell) #config-version=FGT60E-xxx to FGT60F-xxx

claims.claim: BOLL's method copies every line starting with # from the new unit's backup (config-version, conf_file_ver, buildno, global_vdom).
claims.quote: Open this backup with a text editor and copy the lines with a #

claims.claim: BOLL's example header block includes conf_file_ver, buildno and global_vdom lines after config-version.
claims.quote: # conf_file_ver=16381207134220940 # buildno=1828 # global_vdom=1

claims.claim: Owners report mapping 60E ports 6 and 7 to 60F ports A and B (search result text for this thread).
claims.quote: 60E has ports 6 & 7, you need to map them to port A & B on the 60F

claims.claim: Rich-text editors can corrupt the config file.
claims.quote: Do not use rich-text editors because formatting functions can replace ASCII characters or introduce encoding changes.

claims.claim: The default hardware switch is named internal or lan depending on model (search result text for this page).
claims.quote: Supported FortiGate models have a default hardware switch called either internal or lan.

claims.claim: Interface references can sit in policies, routes, SD-WAN, IPsec, zones, DHCP servers, VIPs and local-in policies.
claims.quote: Interface references can exist in firewall policies, static routes, policy routes, SD-WAN, IPsec VPN, zones, DHCP servers, VIPs, local-in policies, dynamic routing protocols, and other configuration sections.

claims.claim: diagnose sys cmdb refcnt show system.interface.name lists what references an interface.
claims.quote: diagnose sys cmdb refcnt show system.interface.name <INTERFACE>

claims.claim: Hardware switches can be listed with show system interface and grep.
claims.quote: show system interface | grep -f 'set type hard-switch'

claims.claim: Individual sections can be migrated by copying them from the old backup.
claims.quote: Individual configuration sections can be manually migrated by copying the required configuration from the source backup configuration file to the destination configuration file.

claims.quote: Register your device to access FortiGuard updates, cloud management, firmware upgrades, technical support and warranty coverage.

claims.quote: Upgrade the new FortiGate device to the same firmware version as the old FortiGate device.
